tax.tagRules:
EXAM (e): canonical values are "INI-CET" and "NEET PG" (exact case as in bank). INI-CET runs two sittings per year since 2021 (May and November); NEET PG has one annual sitting. In orig_bank.json, e is ALREADY correct per src: src=inicet => e=INI-CET; all else => e=NEET PG. NO e relabeling is warranted by exam identity. However, INI-CET questions for plain "2021".."2025" (41+92+102+79+50 = 364 Qs) are y-normalization errors: INI-CET has no bare-year papers, only MAY/November sittings; those bare-year rows (src=inicet, y in {2021,2022,2023,2024,2025}) should be remapped to a specific sitting — MAY 2025 if it is the source PDF's only bare-year series, else flag for manual audit. Realistic options: remap bare INI-CET years to MAY <year> (2021->MAY 2021, etc.), matching the NEET PG bare-year convention (NEET PG 2021 = January 2021 sitting) — but the source PDF (inicet-yearwise.txt) is May + November 2021-2025, so bare years are ambiguous and are likely mid-way extraction of the May series; do NOT guess; flag ~364 Qs for audit. NEET PG y=2026 (200 Qs, src=generated, from paper_2026) is a synthetic mock, keep y=2026 but tag as generated.

YEAR (y): canonical forms: "2021".."2026" (bare, for NEET PG annual sittings and synthetic papers) and "MAY 2021".."MAY 2025", "NOV 2020".."NOV 2024" (for INI-CET sittings). Normalize: uppercase month, single space, 4-digit year ("may 2024"->"MAY 2024", "nov-2022"->"NOV 2022"). NEET PG years must be bare 4-digit; any NEET PG row with "MAY"/"NOV" prefix is a misassignment (should be e=INI-CET or y stripped). The INI-CET May 2025 sitting is the newest real paper in the bank; nothing newer exists.

SRC (question source provenance, keep values verbatim, do NOT relabel): (1) "inicet" (2133 Qs) — parsed directly from the MEDINK INI-CET PYQ PDF (inicet-yearwise.txt): hand-verified previous-year INI-CET questions, both MAY and NOV sittings 2020-2025; highest provenance, only relabel if a dedup check shows the same stem in NEET PG. (2) "curated" (194 Qs) — hand-picked NEET PG PYQs (from neetpg-yearwise.txt MEDINK PDF) plus hand-authored questions; high provenance; check tp against canonical list. (3) "expand" (442 Qs) — workflow-generated recall/revision questions from deep-research expansion (see research/combined-sources.md); NEET PG e; tp is LLM-assigned, highest suspicion for subject/topic drift, re-map via taxonomy; (4) "generated" (200 Qs) — the synthetic NEET PG 2026 mock paper (add_paper2026.py, research/paper_2026); self-authored simulation, keep y=2026. A 5th tag "medink" exists in merge scripts (merge_bank.py, merge_topics2.py) for PDF-parsed NEET PG questions — in orig_bank.json those were folded into curated; if re-introduced, medink and curated are synonyms. src does NOT determine e (except inicet->INI-CET); e determines provenance expectations, not vice versa.
tax.topicNormalization: Apply per topic string, in this order: (1) Strip trailing "(Q-NNN)" / "(Q123)" / "Q-NNN" suffixes — none present in orig_bank.json today (regex audit found 0 hits) but rule guards future merges; also strip other parenthetical exam-reference suffixes like "(NEET 2023)". (2) Keep parenthetical disambiguators that carry meaning, e.g. "Biostatistics (Paired t-test)", "Pyriform Fossa (Nerve Supply)", "HIV Prevention (NACO Guidelines)" — do NOT strip all parens; after canonical topic mapping, fold "(...)" variants into the parent topic ("Biostatistics") or a standard sub-topic. (3) Collapse whitespace: strip leading/trailing, any internal run of spaces/tabs -> single space (audit: 0 violations today). (4) Case: Title Case for the canonical topic name; match case-insensitively against the canonical list, then apply the canonical casing. (5) Sub-topic vs topic granularity: map each string to the BEST canonical topic via longest-substring / keyword match (e.g. "Fracture Neck of Femur" -> "Fracture Neck of Femur" if present else "Lower Limb Fractures"); if no canonical topic matches, keep the string as-is as an extension topic and log it, do not fabricate a parent. (6) Cross-subject overlaps are legitimate and shared topics live in both lists (Dermatology overlaps: Medicine "Infectious Disease" vs Dermatology "STD & Venereology", Paediatrics "Kawasaki Disease", Surgery "Burns" vs Medicine "Burns" — present in both canonical lists; when a question's s is correct, use that subject's canonical list and do not migrate the question to the other subject). (7) Topic is a per-question tag, not a hierarchical path; no slash/arrow separators. (8) After mapping, expect ~19 subjects x ~20-60 topics each (taxonomy has 19 subjects, ~50-68 canonical topics each); residual unmatched strings are the extension surface to review.
notes: orig_bank.json is a list of 2969 dicts: {e, y, s, q, o, a, ex, src, img, tp, qid}; e in {INI-CET, NEET PG}, y in {2021..2026, MAY 2021-2025, NOV 2020-2024}, s is one of exactly 19 subject names (no variants in data), src in {inicet, expand, generated, curated}.

Questions/core_btr.js (7158 Qs, 20 image-based, from a second PDF) is a separate bank — if the taxonomy is applied there too, expect different subject list (core BTR 19+ subjects); this taxonomy covers orig_bank.json's 19.
NEET PG 2026 mock (generated) is a synthetic paper for practice — mark it separately from real 2021-2025 PYQs in any year filter UI.

Topic list in this taxonomy is the canonical NEET-PG-standard set (based on MEDINK/NODIA PYQ layout per research/neetpg-yearwise.txt and inicet-yearwise.txt); each subject has ~50-68 topics — above the 20-50 target because question text is heterogeneous; trim to 20-50 if UI space demands, keeping the most frequent topics per subject (frequency data available in orig_bank.json).
INI-CET did not exist before Nov 2020 (first INI-CET was Nov 2020), so e=INI-CET with y<2020 is impossible; NEET PG 2026 mock is the only y=2026 row.
